$comment: The sample church's two step programs (decisions 83 to 89, and docs/steps.md): the adult Discipleship Path and the Student Path. Rock's Discipleship Path, its four step types, and their Guids are kept and updated in place (rockProgram and rockType true); every other program and type is new. Every step comes from a record the data already has: each step type's 'source' says which one. The rates are designed targets, not measured ones (decision 89). Step type keys are unique across programs.
$objectivesComment: Rock's Organizational Objective defined values, by the key each step type names.

programs.name: Discipleship Path
programs.description: The steps we hope every adult takes: belong in a group, grow in faith, contribute by serving and giving, and lead others.
programs.$completionFlowComment: Rock's Linear (Preferred): the order is a suggestion, and Rock still shows and enforces the prerequisites below.

statuses.$comment: Rock's two Discipleship Path statuses. A rhythm step is Complete from the day it starts (decision 86).

programs.$prerequisitesComment: Rock's one prerequisite is kept: Serve requires a completed Starting Point Class.
programs.$stepTypesComment: In path order, which is also each type's Order in Rock. 'stage' is the Ministry by Design stage and is not stored in Rock. A Rock type with no description keeps Rock's. 'engagement' is Milestone (happens once) or Rhythm (a habit that starts and can stop). 'impact' is Rock's impact weight, 1 to 5.

source.$scheduleComment: Each campus runs a class every four weeks on four Wednesday nights. The current class started one to two weeks before the install day, so a few people at every campus are In Progress on any day.
source.$whoComment: Every volunteer has one before their first Serve step (the prerequisite). Then adults in a group, then other active adults, until percentOfActiveAdults of active adults have one.
source.$nearComment: Taken in the daysBefore days before the person's first group or team.
source.$otherwiseComment: Without a group or team: within daysAfter days of the household's first visit, or any time in the history window when the first visit is before it.

source.$comment: One step per small group membership, from the day the person joined to the day they left. A pending request is not a step.

The step and Rock's Baptism Date person attribute always agree. The Cast's dates come from their household files; generated adults get dates here. Baptized Here (on the step and on the person) is Yes when the baptism came after the household's first visit.
source.$ratesComment: Shares of generated adults with a baptism. Volunteers and leaders are more often baptized, and other active adults make up the rest of percentOfActiveAdults.
source.$sundaysComment: Most baptisms here happen on the church's baptism Sundays: Easter, and the given week's Sunday of a summer month.
source.$studentsComment: A student's baptism goes on this step too (decision 87). Students are the children who checked in to the Student Path's student service. afterPercent of the students with an afterStepType step are baptized here on the first baptism Sunday at least minimumDaysAfter days after it, when that Sunday has come by the install day. percentOfOtherStudents of the other students are baptized here on a baptism Sunday after their first student check-in. Every student baptism is here, at hereMinimumAge or older. A Cast file's Baptism Date is kept as it is. The adult rates above are unchanged by students.

stepTypes.name: Foundations
stepTypes.description: Foundations is a six-week course on what Christians believe, how to read the Bible, and how to pray. It gives a firm footing for a life of following Jesus.
stepTypes.callToActionDescription: A new course starts every eight weeks at every campus. Sign up at the Welcome Center or online.

source.$scheduleComment: Each campus runs a six-week course on Tuesday nights, starting every eight weeks. The current course started two to three weeks before the install day.
source.$preferComment: Leaders and volunteers take it first, as many churches ask of them.
source.$nearComment: Often in the person's first year in a group.

source.$comment: One step per serving team membership. A volunteer who waits as Pending (decision 72) is In Progress; the step becomes Complete the day they become Active.

stepTypes.name: Give
stepTypes.description: Generous giving is part of how we take part in God's mission. This step marks giving to the church regularly and consistently.
stepTypes.callToActionDescription: Set up a recurring gift online in a few minutes, or give in the offering on Sunday.

source.$comment: From Rock's giving journey stages, run every Tuesday night the way Rock's Giving Automation job runs them (decision 85). A step starts the week a giver becomes Consistent and ends the week they become Lapsed or Former. A giver who comes back gets a new step.

stepTypes.name: Lead
stepTypes.description: Leaders help others grow and take their next step. This step marks leading a small group or a serving team.
stepTypes.callToActionDescription: Talk with a staff member about leading a small group or a serving team.

source.$comment: One step per membership in a leader role, on a small group or a serving team.

programs.name: Student Path
programs.$categoryComment: Rock's Discipleship step program category, where Rock files the Discipleship Path.
programs.description: The steps we hope every student takes: come to camp, decide to follow Jesus, serve on a mission trip, and help lead younger students.

statuses.$comment: The Student Path's own statuses, named and colored like Rock's, since a Rock status belongs to one program.

students.$comment: Who the program is for: people who check in to the student service, in these check-in groups from configuration/checkin.json. A student's grade on a day comes from their graduation year, moving up the day after each June 1, as Rock does. Someone has been attending when they checked in to the student service at least checkIns times in the withinDays days before. Each step's percentOfStudents is a share of the students who could take it, rounded, counted for the Cast and the generated households on their own; a Cast story counts toward it.

programs.$stepTypesComment: Steps happen only inside the history window, and only while the person was a student who had been attending.

stepTypes.name: Student Camp
stepTypes.description: Student Camp is a week away each summer to have fun, make friends, and hear about Jesus. For many students it is their first step.
stepTypes.callToActionDescription: Camp is a week in late June for students in grades 7 to 12. Sign up in the student lobby or online.

source.$comment: One church-wide camp each summer, Monday to Friday, starting on the given Monday of June. A student could go when they were in these grades on camp's first day and had been attending. percentOfStudents of the students who could go to one or more camps go once, in one of those summers, and then again in each later summer they could, againPercent of the time.

stepTypes.name: Follow Jesus
stepTypes.description: Follow Jesus marks a student's decision to put their trust in Jesus and follow him.
stepTypes.callToActionDescription: If you have decided to follow Jesus, or want to talk about it, find a student leader after the service.

source.$comment: percentOfStudents of students make the decision once. A student who went to camp makes it there atEvent.percent of the time, on a day of one of their camps. Otherwise it falls on a Sunday they checked in to the student service: Easter easterPercent of the time when they came that Easter, and any other such Sunday otherwise.

stepTypes.name: Mission Trip
stepTypes.description: On a mission trip, high school students serve alongside a partner church and see God at work in another place.
stepTypes.callToActionDescription: High school students can go over spring break or in the summer. Ask a student leader about the next trip.

source.$comment: Two church-wide trips a year: one over spring break, one in the summer, Saturday to Saturday. percentOfStudents of the high school students who could go on one or more trips go on one, and then on one trip in each later calendar year they could, againPercent of the time.

stepTypes.name: Student Leader
stepTypes.description: Student leaders are juniors and seniors who help lead younger students in worship, small group time, and welcome.
stepTypes.callToActionLabel: Apply to Be a Student Leader
stepTypes.callToActionDescription: Juniors and seniors can apply each spring to lead the next school year.

source.$comment: A student could lead when they were in these grades at a school year's start (startsOn) and had been attending. percentOfStudents of them become leaders at the first such start. The step ends at graduation (endsOn in their graduation year), and stays open while they are still in school.
